contract_plain_english: In an Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,p), let d = (n - 1)p be the common expected degree and let d_i be the degree of vertex i. For every vertex i, the preceding Chernoff argument gives the same estimate P(|d_i - d| >= 0.1d) <= 2e^{-cd}, where c is some positive absolute constant. Applying the union bound to the n vertexwise bad events yields P(there is an i from 1 to n with |d_i - d| >= 0.1d) <= the sum of their probabilities, and applying the common estimate to all n summands bounds that sum by n * 2e^{-cd}. This step does not require the vertexwise bad events to be independent and does not yet require d >= C log n; that later condition is used only to convert the expression into the numerical probability bound 0.1.
